claims.content: Today, more than half of Brazilians are overweight and have an associated comorbidity.
Around 20% of Brazilians are in the obesity range.
Weight-loss medications are commonly known as weight-loss pens.
Liraglutide is one of the weight-loss medications approved in Brazil.
Liraglutide is sold under the brand name Saxenda.
Semaglutide is one of the weight-loss medications approved in Brazil.
Semaglutide is known as Wegovy and Ozempic.
Tirzepatide is one of the weight-loss medications approved in Brazil.
Tirzepatide is sold as Mounjaro.
The human body does everything it can to maintain the weight gained when a person gains weight.
The human body maintains weight regardless of how much a person exercises or how little they eat.
Weight-loss medications make a person feel less hungry and become full more quickly.
Weight-loss medications are like a kick-start, but the treatment is much more complex than that.
Weight-loss medication alone is not enough to treat obesity.
A person needs to change their lifestyle as a whole by adjusting their diet and exercising to treat obesity.
Obesity is a chronic disease, similar to diabetes or hypertension.
A person will not be cured of obesity even after losing weight.
A person may regain weight at any time even after losing weight.
The assessment of which weight-loss medication is most appropriate for a person's case must be individualized and performed by a physician.
Weight-loss medications are sold only with a prescription to protect the patient's health.
Improper use of weight-loss medications without medical guidance can cause adverse effects.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience unpleasant side effects.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience drug interactions.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience excessive loss of muscle mass known as sarcopenia.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience hair loss.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience brittle nails.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience malnutrition.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience pancreatic toxicity.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own face the risk of obtaining counterfeit medications.
In the long term, a person seeking weight-loss treatment on their own may lose weight but may also lose their health.
Weight-loss medications can help people who need them.
The goal of weight-loss medications is not to help a person lose a few pounds for aesthetic reasons.
The goal of weight-loss medications is to restore health and quality of life.
